items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Benner' only in the phrase 'after Benner had gone to work' as a temporal marker for an incident involving Don Byas and Count Basie. There is no direct interaction, personal connection, or professional relationship described between Buddy Tate and Benner.

ctx.x: So the cats, "Man, I never heard nothing like that on saxophone in my life. Gee, this cat --" Man, they was talking like that and Don got stoned, you know. He just got so jealous. He went over there and he got ossified. I mean,

he couldn't hit the ground with his head. So he come back and Basie says, "You're drunk." This is after Benner had gone to work. He says, -- he didn't say anything then. So they he says, "You're drunk." He says, "Yes, and you're the cause of it. And all of you son of a bitches," you know, that's what he called all of us. "Goddamn," he says, "you're raving over him. Wasn't worth a damn thing, he was playing," you know. And one word brought on -- you know, they said -- that's what ya say something.

So, man, before we know anything, he jumped back against the wall, Gary, and pulled a little owl-head about that long. He said, "I don't want the son of a bitch to say nothing to me. I'll kill everybody." He's stoned, man. So I says, "Shit, maybe he will. He don't know what the hell he's going. He's drunk." Now he's too far to rush, you know, there's not anyplace you can grab.
